description.narrative: The program will support the implementation of key policy and institutional reforms, particularly the Rice Tarrification Act and its associated reforms and programs. As the reforms are wide and deep in their impact, it is important that the government will continue to earn support to the reforms from the people of the Philippines.

description.narrative:

b. Growth in the Value of Agriculture and Fishery Exports (year-on-year, FOB value, in percent) increased to 9% (2017 baseline: - 2.85%)

Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Agricultural trade policy and regulatory framework. Indicator: The government dismantled the state monopoly on rice and improved food governance by removing the regulatory powers and commercial functions of the NFA and transforming it into an emergency buffer stock management agency. Data Source: Legislative Report in Official Gazette Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Target year: 2023 Target value: Y

Output: Agricultural trade policy and regulatory framework. Indicator: The government facilitated agricultural trade by removing nontariff barriers and streamlining administrative procedures on agricultural imports, and rolled out its online trade facilitation portal, TradeNet, with the Department of Agriculture as a key regulatory agency. Data Source: Legislative Report in Official Gazette, DOF reports Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Target year: 2023 Target value: Y

Output: Agricultural trade policy and regulatory framework. Indicator: The government removed quantitative restrictions on rice imports, converting them to a simple tariff system to improve food security by increasing rice availability for all Filipinos, and to reduce poverty by increasing disposable income through affordable rice prices. Data Source: Legislative Report in Official Gazette Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Target year: 2023 Target value: Y

Output: Public services and finance to the agriculture sector Indicator: To address fragmented and uncoordinated water resources management, the government (i) established the National Water Management Council; and (ii) submitted legislation to Congress to create the Department of Water Resources for integrated planning, policy formulation, and management of water resources that incorporates gender equality, social inclusion, climate resiliency, and disaster risk reduction. Data Source: Philippine House of Representatives website Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Target year: 2020 Target value: Y

Output: Public services and finance to the agriculture sector Indicator: To improve rice sector competitiveness under the liberalized trade regime, the government (i) established the RCEF in 57 potential rice-competitive provinces during 2019-2025 and (ii) allocated ₱10 billion in the 2019 and 2020 GAAs. Data Source: Department of Agriculture website Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Target year: 2020 Target value: Y

Output: Public services and finance to the agriculture sector Indicator: To improve the country's irrigation systems and expand service areas, the government (through the National Economic Development Authority) developed the national irrigation master plan; and all concerned government agencies, spearheaded by the National Irrigation Administration, adopted it. Data Source: National Irrigation Authority website Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Target year: 2020 Target value: Y

Output: Public services and finance to the agriculture sector Indicator: To reduce flood risk, the government (through the Department of Public Works and Highways) developed flood risk management master plans for six major river basins, integrating flood protection infrastructure with enhanced flood resilience and response measures and climate adaptation in consultation with basin stakeholders. Data Source: Legislative Report in Official Gazette, Department of Agriculture website Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Target year: 2020 Target value: Y

Output: Public services and finance to the agriculture sector Indicator: To remove restrictions on agricultural land ownership, the government enacted the Agricultural Free Patent Reform Act, 2019—allowing farmers to make their land titles immediately tradeable and bankable, providing them access to capital and credit. Data Source: Legislative Report in Official Gazette Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Target year: 2020 Target value: Y

Output: Social protection for rural families Indicator: As targeted support for small rice farmers (1 hectare or less), through the Department of Agriculture's Agriculture Credit Policy Council, the government established SURE Aid to provide interest-free loans and allocated ₱2.5 billion in the 2020 GAA, maintaining a sex-disaggregated list of beneficiaries. Data Source: Department of Agriculture website Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Target year: 2020 Target value: Y

Output: Social protection for rural families Indicator: To address access to basic needs (health, education, nutrition) of the poor, the government institutionalized the conditional cash transfer program (4Ps), which increases health and education grant rates in the benefits package to promote prenatal services for pregnant women, empowerment of women and children's rights; achieve universal primary education; reduce child mortality and malnutrition; and improve the maternal health of the poor. Data Source: Legislative Report in Official Gazette, DSWD reports Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Target year: 2020 Target value: Y

Output: Social protection for rural families Indicator: To improve children's nutrition in poor households, as well as their health and wellbeing, the government enacted the Act Institutionalizing a National Feeding Program for Undernourished Children in Public Day Care, Kindergarten and Elementary Schools and allocated ₱3.6 billion in the 2020 GAA. Data Source: Legislative Report in Official Gazette, DepED, DSWD reports Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Target year: 2020 Target value: Y

Output: Social protection for rural families Indicator: To support rice farmers (including women) affected by declining farmgate rice prices, the government established an unconditional cash transfer program and allocated ₱3.0 billion in 2019, maintaining a sex-disaggregated list of beneficiaries. Data Source: Department of Agriculture website Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2018 Baseline value: N Target year: 2020 Target value: Y
